what_happened: Task 348's file_scope (set at task creation) already locked the exact four paths and the settings-fragment filename/location, which the dispatch had framed as an open naming decision for research/plan to settle -- confirming this via a direct read of specs/state.json saved a full design-space exploration round.

The dispatch's acceptance requires confirming the hook ACTUALLY FIRES after a real deploy, but the harness's own PreToolUse dispatch can only be observed from a session whose project directory is the consumer repo (/home/benjamin/Projects/Logos/Verification); the books extension is not loaded in this nvim config repo (extensions: core, email, lean, literature, memory, nix, nvim), so an implementation dispatch running here cannot trigger it end to end. The plan's Phase 5 substitutes driving the DEPLOYED hook copy with a real PreToolUse payload against a real committed evidence file, plus independent jq proof that the registration is bare and joined to the single Write-Edit matcher block, and records the residual with an operator reproduction recipe.

The consumer repository was locatable and directly readable during planning, so every registration premise was re-confirmed against the LIVE deployed settings file rather than inferred: its .claude/settings.json already carries an exact-string Write-Edit PreToolUse block with validate-no-task-references.sh (the block to join) AND a separate legacy Write-only block, which is a live in-repo demonstration of the near-miss-spelling hazard the dispatch warns about. The 7814-character longest line in 01-book-identity-and-membership.md was also re-measured, grounding the buried-long-line fixture.

Phase 1 hook (validate-evidence-append-only.sh) passed shellcheck and all manual smoke-test cases (truncation refused exit 2, pure append/out-of-scope/README.md allowed exit 0) on first write, no iteration needed.

While designing Phase 2's Ruling-2 fixture (in-place edit to an uncommitted trailing entry, not merely an append), found the Phase 1 hook's Edit predicate (old_string suffix-of-HEAD-baseline) would incorrectly REFUSE that case, since typo-fix text in the uncommitted tail never appears in the HEAD baseline at all. Fixed by splitting the baseline into FLOOR (HEAD) vs DISK (current on-disk) vs TAIL (DISK minus FLOOR prefix), with two Edit allow-patterns: (a) pure append relative to DISK, (b) free edit confined to TAIL. Re-verified with 5 scratch-repo smoke cases including the companion refusal (edit spanning floor+tail) and the non-git fallback. No scope or file-list change.
